provider: LINE Messaging API — message content endpoint

free_tier.stated: No storage quota is offered at all. Content is a delivery mechanism, not a store.
free_tier.notes: the headline offer as the seed recorded it; the binding constraint is in limits[]

per_object_cap.stated: no per-object cap was extracted from the seed's quota and limits prose; absence here is a gap in this conversion, not a vendor claim that no cap exists
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: no retention statement was extracted from the seed's quota and limits prose; absence here is a gap in this conversion, not a vendor claim that retention is unlimited
retention.notes: extraction found no retention clause; the seed's limits text may still state one, see extras.limits_verbatim

egress.terms: Retrieval is authenticated only: GET /v2/bot/message/{messageId}/content with a channel access token. No public URL is ever issued.

tooling: line-bot-sdk (Python/Node/Java/Go/PHP). The SDK exposes get_message_content() and nothing else — no listing, no expiry control, no bulk export.
chaining: Not chainable: there is no enumeration API, so you cannot even address stored objects after the fact without having logged every messageId yourself.
limits_note: Explicit auto-deletion with an undisclosed period: 'Content that users send is automatically deleted after a certain period of time.' LINE does not publish the number, which is worse than a known 30 days because it cannot be reasoned about. No listing endpoint, no bulk download.
